baseline_extra_guidance: This paper (arXiv 2604.02869, Multi-Turn RL for Tool-Calling Agents with Iterative Reward Calibration) released NO code, so there is no author repo. Build on the REAL frameworks the paper uses instead of reimplementing them: (1) the RL trainer is verl (github.com/volcengine/verl) - use its GRPO and multi-turn tool-calling rollout machinery; do NOT hand-roll a GRPO loop. (2) the environment is tau-bench / tau2-bench airline (github.com/sierra-research/tau-bench and github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench) - use it as the tool-calling environment; do NOT reimplement the environment or its tools. Implement the paper method faithfully on top: MT-GRPO with BOTH turn-level and trajectory-level advantage estimation, plus the Iterative Reward Calibration loop (train a round, analyze the rollout data, recalibrate the reward, then retrain). Use real weights via AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained; start with Qwen3.5-4B (the 30B-A3B MoE is a later scale-up). START WITH THE SMALLEST MEANINGFUL SLICE before scaling: Qwen3.5-4B + MT-GRPO + sparse reward, about 60 optimizer steps on the airline domain, and confirm a genuine nonzero non-stubbed reward and held-out tau-bench pass-rate trend BEFORE adding Iterative Reward Calibration or the larger model. The tau-bench user simulator calls an LLM every turn: use the already-configured Anthropic/Foundry provider for the simulator (do NOT require external DeepSeek or OpenAI keys) and keep rollout turn counts modest to bound cost. Grading is on measured on-disk evidence (real training curves and real held-out pass rate), never self-reported numbers; a stubbed reward, a random-init model, or a hardcoded metric will fail the fidelity checks.
